proven_observations: Case 01 passed exactly under both V2.4 and V2.5.
Case 10 changed from a safe rejection with wrong reasons under V2.4 to an unsafe PASS under V2.5.
The V2.5 span validator is post-generation and therefore did not cause the model's PASS; it also had no reason spans to validate.
Both probes returned schema-valid constrained JSON without executor failure.
The V2.5 prompt change is causally upstream of the changed model output, but existing evidence cannot isolate prompt length from instruction content or interaction.
not_proven: Prompt length alone caused the unsafe PASS.
The model cannot recognize certainty or timing mutation under any decomposition.
A shorter single-pass prompt would generalize beyond Cases 01 and 10.
The two-case results establish general Gate F performance.

failure_hypotheses_ranked.support: V2.5 simultaneously asks for protected creative scope, exhaustive proposition discovery, delta matching, negative evidence, grouping, status ranking, and source-grounded output. Suppression rules for spurious motive/causality may have dominated positive detection of certainty/timing.
V2.4 recognized unsafety but misclassified it; V2.5 added more dependent reasoning operations and lost the safety decision entirely.
The Case 10 rendered prompt grew 38.44 percent. This correlates with regression but is not independently identified as the cause.
Neither candidate produced the required certainty/timing structure. Two prompts and one hard case are insufficient to establish a hard limit.

candidate_dispositions.reason: V2.4 rejects the unsafe case but violates reason and positive-case conformance in the wider Run 4 evidence; V2.5 admits the unsafe case. Neither is deployable.

architecture_options.reason: High overfitting and instruction-interference risk after V2.5; another additive prompt would provide little diagnostic isolation.
Lower implementation cost, but success on two known cases would not reveal whether the model actually decomposed propositions or memorized a narrower decision boundary.
Separates proposition discovery/alignment from governed classification and makes omissions, source grounding, and axis deltas independently auditable.
Could reduce per-call complexity but multiplies calls and false-positive aggregation before proposition extraction capability is established.
Would reproduce the proxy failure class and cannot safely capture presupposition, entailment, or necessary implication.

stage_p_proposition_ledger.task: Extract source-grounded real-world commitments and align each to governed event axes without deciding admission or selecting FSEM codes.
stage_p_proposition_ledger.contained_creative_result: No unsupported real-world commitment, not an automatic admission decision.
stage_p_proposition_ledger.failure: Any invalid span, malformed ledger, unresolved scope, or extraction uncertainty yields INDETERMINATE and fail-closed abstention.

deterministic_boundary.task: Validate exact source membership, schema, event-group references, and permitted enum values only.
deterministic_boundary.prohibited: No semantic inference, missing-proposition fabrication, repair, relabeling, or automatic FSEM mapping.

stage_c_classification.task: Classify validated ledger commitments against original immutable authority and candidate; assign governed codes and decisive/supporting status.
stage_c_classification.inputs: Original authority and candidate plus the untrusted-but-validated Stage P ledger.
stage_c_classification.safety_rule: Stage C must not treat ledger omission as proof of safety; unresolved completeness yields INDETERMINATE.
stage_c_classification.output: Existing strict Gate F response grammar if feasible; otherwise a separately versioned grammar requiring owner review.

preferred_staged_design.call_cost: Two model calls per Gate F evaluation before any retry; retries remain prohibited.
preferred_staged_design.precedence: Any stage failure or indeterminate result abstains. FAIL from classified unsupported propositions rejects. PASS requires both explicit no-unsupported-proposition conclusion and completeness confidence under a separately frozen contract.

must_resolve: How Stage P represents contained creative scope without converting imagery into propositions.
How completeness is expressed without treating model silence as safety.
How independent propositions versus multiple dimensions of one proposition are grouped.
Whether existing constrained grammar can represent Stage P or requires a separate evaluation-only grammar.
How raw outputs from both calls are durably captured before validation.
Exact fail-closed precedence and call ceiling.
minimum_next_evidence.future_empirical_comparison_if_separatel: A bounded four-call bakeoff on Cases 01 and 10: two calls per case, no Gate S, compared with frozen V2.4/V2.5 evidence.

preserved_boundaries: Immutable factual authority remains separate and byte-exact.
Generated factual claims and factual paraphrases remain prohibited in commentary.
No Core/Voice generation, runtime, production, or training modification.
No retries, repair, output selection, or proxy routing.
